title: Signed coordinates for symbolic answers
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $W$ be a natural number. Suppose a table of Boolean answers satisfies every checker condition for all $t,a<2^W$ and $j\le |x|+1$, using the supplied input-bit function. For every selector $\tau$, time $t<2^W$, Boolean sign $s$, and natural number $a$, the symbolic answer at coordinates $(t,a)$ equals the answer at time $t$ and signed integer coordinate $(-1)^s a$, where the sign convention is $(-1)^{\mathrm{false}}a=a$ and $(-1)^{\mathrm{true}}a=-a$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite-tape machine over Boolean symbols
A Boolean input word and a natural number width W
The answer table satisfies every checker condition for all t,a<2^W and j≤|x|+1, with the supplied input-bit function
The time coordinate t is less than 2^W
A selector τ that is absent or names one of the machine's work tapes
A Boolean sign s and natural number a
